newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade thin.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in late trading on Friday after dipping in the early session as demand remained weak, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,425-30 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but offers were heard at five rupiah above and below the range.
Crude palm oil was last done at an equivalent of 1,259 rupiah/kg at a 1,000-tonne tender in the North Sumatran city of Medan on Thursday. It was on offer at 1,260 rupiah.
"The market finished the week as it began...quietly. But I think demand should pick up next week," one trader said.
Sellers are hoping consumer demand will pick up as Moslems begin to stock up cooking oil ahead of the Eid al-Fitr celebrations on February 9 and 10.
They also said the relatively high price of crude palm oil was keeping olein processing margins thin, but added that crude palm oil export prices were attractive.
"Export prices are looking good despite a relatively high export tax expected in February," one said.
Initial concern by buyers following Thursday's riots in west Java had subsided. A mob of Moslems wrecked buildings and cars in the incident after a reported insult against Islam.
